text.p: London-based Paribas Capital Markets said on Tuesday it was reinforcing its "buy" position on German retailer Metro AG following the sale of its Moebel Unger furniture unit and the purchase of PC retailer Peacock.
Paribas said in an investment note its price target for Metro stood 25 percent higher than the stock's current level.
Metro shares earlier closed bourse trade one mark higher at 168 after it said it would take an extraordinary charge of 190 million marks related to the sale of Moebel Unger.
The group also said its Vobis Microcomputer AG unit would take over rival PC retailer Peacock AG.
"Both deals are very good news for the stock in terms of sentiment, as it illustrates the management's dedication to restructuring the business," Paribas said in the note.
The bank said it expected the the deals overall to be earnings-enhancing for 1997 and increased its 1997 earnings per share forecast from 9.79 marks to 10.26.
